title: So-Called Work
description: After having made one mistake too many at work, Linling is in danger of losing her job...

mainQuestExcel.title: So-Called Work
mainQuestExcel.description: After having made one mistake too many at work, Linling is in danger of losing her job...

dialogs.text: I'm finished, it's all over for me this time...
What's wrong?
*sobs* Nervous An said that I might not be cut out for this line of work...
Isn't he just firing me? What do I do? I... I'm always working so hard...
Huh? Why so sudden...
Well... Didn't I ask you before to help me count boats?
I trusted in your ability, so I didn't double check the data you gave me, and handed it in directly.
A lot of the numbers turned out to be wrong... Nervous An really lost his temper.
Won't you help me talk to him? I—I'll do my job seriously from now on! And I won't call on you to help me out again, either!
But I dare not go to ask him myself...
Were the previous boat tallies wrong?
Yes! Didn't I ask you to help me out with them before?
I trusted in your ability, so I didn't double check the data. I handed it in directly... and a lot of it turned out to be wrong.
But I only asked for your help from time to time. I also tallied a great deal of numbers myself...
So when put side by side, I didn't know where I had gone wrong at all, which made Nervous An lose his temper...
Please help me talk to him! I—I'll do my job seriously from now on! And I won't ask you to help me out again, either!
But I dare not go to ask him myself...
*sigh* Really, this is...
Can we talk about Linling?
Hmm? You're asking about Linling? Well... How do I say this? She's just not really suited for her job.
Specifically, the mistakes she's made in her data entry are far too egregious.
As for this week's data, only one or two days out of seven have the correct numbers. Even a purely visual inspection would be more accurate.
How can I leave this job to her with that attitude?
Well, if it's just numbers...
There is no "just" when it comes to work.
If a single plank in a wooden barrel is a little short, then the volume of the whole barrel goes down.
It is the same with work. If we get careless about even one matter, we will drag the larger work through the mud.
Let's take tallying up the number of boats, for example. If the numbers are not accurate, then the various activities we conduct at the harbor will also be imprecise.
Imprecision there can be costly, and even if someone remedies the issue, the time unnecessarily lost fixing the problem cannot be gained back.
Do you understand now?
I... I understand.
Still, we do lack manpower here at the harbor, so I most likely won't fire her.
How should I put it... "a plank shorter" is better than "a plank short," no?
The person in charge of reviewing cargo is unable to be here due to an emergency. Tell Linling that her help there will be expedient.
If nothing serious goes wrong with her work there, then she can return to her job tallying boats when the person in charge of the review returns to work.
Hmm... I guess this can be considered a test, and something of a second chance.
Give this manifest to Linling. Ask her to conduct checks according to it, and make markings on the back once each check is completed.
Also, please tell her to pull her socks up. If she slips up here as well, then there won't be any more second chances.
I'll go tell her...
What will you tell her? That she's fired? No, she's not fired just yet.
We have a dire lack of manpower here at the harbor. How do I say this... "a plank shorter" is still better than "a plank short," yes?
The person in charge of reviewing cargo is unable to be here due to an emergency. Tell Linling that her help there will be expedient.
If nothing serious goes wrong with her work there, then she can return to her job tallying boats when the person in charge of the review returns to work.
...I can't write poetry at work anymore. I've got to focus...
Work comes first in the end.
I know that. But doing the same thing day in, day out, year on year... you eventually get bored, you know?
And, well, it's precisely because it's this kind of sideline job, you know? It's not that important, and no one really pays you mind, so you start to drift off after a while...
Nervous An always says things like "every job is important" and "every job is decisive..."
But if that's the case, why's everyone still so picky about the kind of work they want to do?
You need to take responsibility for your work.
I only ask for your help occasionally. I do it myself most of the time.
I know I should take responsibility for my work. But the busier it gets, the more I feel like slacking off. That's why I ask for your help at times.
If I really were to become idle, I find myself looking for things to do instead...
Well, you haven't worked a day in your life, have you? There's no use telling you all this...
Why do you want to write poetry so much?
Why are you suddenly asking me this? Let me think... Well, why do you think a person works?
The way I see it, "working for the sake of continuing to work" is a little too boring.
How I say this? Everyone has got to have their dreams, right? A dream that's totally separate from the daily drudgery of work.
That way, even in moments when you're so tired that you think you might break, you can take refuge in your dreams.
But this is just my way of thinking, of course. I have no idea how adventurers would think of this problem.
When I look at the way they do nothing but live for their dreams, I feel like I need some kind of daily work to ground myself instead.
Still... Hahaha, take it from me: dreams are just dreams. When you work, you still need to keep your feet firmly planted.
Oh, what shall I do about work...
Nervous An says he's giving you another chance.
Really! Wonderful! That's great!
Eh? A cargo review? Oh no... I've never done that before...
If I make another mistake, I'm definitely finished. No, I have to make preparations first...
I need to find the previous review standards, and also the previous standard formats...
Could you help me confirm the amount of cargo first? You just need to check the cargo numbers against the document and see if they're accurate. I will conduct a more detailed review later.
I got it.
Thank you so much. I'll be making preparations here in the meantime.
I can't mess up this time...
You can leave everything to us.
No, I can't, not this time. A cargo review is way more complex than tallying boats. I have to do this myself.
So, please just confirm the amounts of cargo. I will do a more specific review afterwards.
I'm a cooper: I'm neither particularly good with my hands, nor do I have any particular talents.
A cooper?
Well, that is to say that I'm like someone who repairs barrels, and who needs a single plank of wood to finish my wooden barrel.
But the plank I have in hand isn't of good quality. It's just a little short, and if I use it to make my wooden barrel, its capacity is going to be lowered significantly.
Still, if I want to get a new plank, who knows when I will finish that barrel.
And given that the deadline for finishing the barrel is drawing near, I have to choose the lesser of two evils.
Who knows how many people there are under the sun who are coopers like me, who are facing a dilemma similar to mine.
Can we talk about Linling's job?
Her job? Ah, yes. She did ask you to help her tally boat numbers in the past, didn't she? I know about that.
Don't look so surprised. As long as we get results, I'm really not picky as to how she does her work.
Besides, the rewards she gives you are taken out of her own pocket.
But as for her reporting data without reviewing it first...
That irresponsible attitude is what really made me angry.
